LLM auditresponse for .pre-commit-config.yaml:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard `.pre-commit-config.yaml` file used by the AUR dotnet-roslyn package to enforce code quality and packaging checks before commits. The file defines 15+ hooks that use locally installed system tools (shfmt, shellcheck, ruff, biome, b2sum, sha512sum, makepkg, etc.) — no hooks download anything from the internet, and the `no-downloads` hook actively prevents binary files from being committed.

The embedded bash scripts (in the `srcinfo`, `checksums`, `termux-language-server`, `systemd-lsp`, and `psscriptanalyzer` hooks) perform standard packaging verification tasks: verifying `.SRCINFO` is up to date, checking local source file checksums against `.SRCINFO`, and linting various file formats. None of these scripts exfiltrate data, execute downloaded code, use obfuscation, or modify system files outside the repository scope. The code is written in clear, readable bash without any encoding or hidden behavior.

Overall, this file represents legitimate, security-conscious packaging hygiene — it enforces checks rather than introducing vulnerabilities. It follows standard AUR maintainer practices for pre-commit configuration.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>

</security_assessment>
